findings.quote: the sentence on what the timeout covers (today `timeout은 2단계(진행 중인 요청을 기다리는 시간)에만 걸리고`) names the renumbered step, step 3 that waits for in-flight requests within the deadline, instead of `2단계` ... finds that sentence naming `3단계`
findings.description: The iteration-3 fix makes app.md say the timeout applies only to step 3 (the wait for in-flight requests). D-344 and FR-APP-020 count the WebSocket close wait (min(1 s, time left), step 2 of the new list) and the force-close at the deadline (step 4) inside the same deadline (FR-APP-020 AC-2: timeout 500 ms -> close wait ends within 700 ms and shutdown returns within 500 ms + 3 s). A reader of app.md would add up to 1 s of goodbye on top of the timeout, which the code does not do, and lifecycle.md (OPS-APP-005 AC-9) says the opposite. The docs test would lock the wrong sentence in.
findings.suggested_fix: AC-8: "... the sentence on what the timeout covers names steps 2 to 4 (the goodbye, which waits at most 1 s or the time left, the wait for in-flight requests and the force-close at the timeout) as sharing the one timeout, instead of `2단계`, and keeps that `onStop`, closing owned resources and the logger flush have no time limit; a docs test finds that sentence naming `2~4단계`."

findings.quote: the `TestApp.webSocketRoute(path)` fixture keeps its signature and keeps registering through that hook ... The upgrade cases of `HttpAcceptanceTest#sdsAc18_...` ... are re-pointed to this AC and changed to assert the handshake
findings.description: The hook takes a `RouteHandler`, but `app.ws` takes a `WebSocketHandler`; no AC says how `ws` carries its handler through a `RouteHandler`-typed hook, or what the core runs after `101` for a hook route whose `RouteHandler` is not an `app.ws` handler. The fixture registers `(req, res) -> { throw new IllegalStateException("WebSocket hook routes are not dispatched in wave 3"); }` (TestApp.java:48-51), so the re-pointed HttpAcceptanceTest upgrade case could see an open session, a 1011 close (FR-WS-006 AC-10) or a 500, and the expected result of "assert the handshake" is open. The first rationale note ('the TestApp.webSocketRoute fixture move to FR-WS-001') still contradicts the correcting note below it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Decision to AC-7: "`app.ws` passes the hook an internal `RouteHandler` adapter holding its `WebSocketHandler`; for a hook route whose `RouteHandler` is not such an adapter the core completes the upgrade and runs no `ws` handler, never invoking that `RouteHandler`, so the re-pointed fixture cases assert that `HttpExchange.webSocket` was called (over the in-memory adapter: the recorded hand-over) and the fixture's javadoc says wave 7 dispatches the handshake." Drop or mark superseded the first rationale note.

findings.quote: a session whose client sends a Ping frame every 300 ms but no text or binary message is handed close `1001` by the scheduler within 2 s of its last text or binary message
findings.description: The client sends no text or binary message, so 'its last text or binary message' has no time point; the test cannot anchor the 2 s bound.
findings.suggested_fix: "... is handed close `1001` by the scheduler within 2 s of the `101` (no text or binary message is exchanged) ..."

findings.quote: A peer that never answers the close and keeps sending frames keeps the session open ... This is a TinyHttpd gap under D-020, deferred
findings.description: FR-WS-008 records a fourth deferred TinyHttpd gap (a peer that never answers the server's close but keeps sending frames stays open), but OPS-WS-001 AC-3 lists only three deferred limitations for websocket.md, so users are not told that idle/overflow closes depend on the peer answering.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to OPS-WS-001 AC-3: "and that a peer that never answers the server's close frame but keeps sending frames stays open until its own close, shutdown or `writeTimeout` (deferred TinyHttpd limitation)", found by a fixed phrase.

findings.quote: a reflection test asserts the default method and the override

AC-4 names the RestApp set; AC-1 names neither Response change.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-1: "and `HttpApiSurfaceTest`'s Response signature set gains `sse()->SseClient` while its later-wave name list drops `sse` (IR-HTTP-001 AC-3 is stated for the wave 3 merge)."
